_meta.title: AgriTech crop reference library
_meta.source: General agronomy summaries compiled for a student capstone from widely published public extension guidance (e.g. ICAR / state agricultural university crop guides). Values are APPROXIMATE and vary by variety, region and season.
_meta.disclaimer: Educational reference only. Always confirm sowing dates, varieties, doses and pesticide choices with your local Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) or agriculture officer.
_meta.maintain: Edit this file (or move it to a CropInfo collection) to add crops. Each crop needs the same keys.

crops.name: Wheat
crops.overview: A major winter cereal grown across the Indo-Gangetic plain and central India.
crops.climate: Cool weather during growth and warm, dry weather at grain filling; roughly 10-25 °C.
crops.soil: Well-drained loam to clay loam, near neutral pH.
crops.irrigation: Commonly irrigated at critical stages such as crown root initiation, tillering, flowering and grain filling.
crops.planting: Sown typically in November in northern India using certified seed; line sowing is preferred to broadcasting.
crops.harvest: When the grain is hard and the crop turns golden-yellow and dry.
care: Control weeds in the first 30-40 days

pests.name: Yellow rust
pests.symptoms: Yellow stripes of powdery spores on leaves.
pests.prevention: Resistant varieties, timely sowing, monitor in cool humid weather and consult an officer on fungicide use.

pests.name: Aphids
pests.symptoms: Clusters of small insects on leaves and ear heads; sticky honeydew.
pests.prevention: Field scouting, avoid excess nitrogen, encourage natural enemies.

crops.name: Rice (Paddy)
crops.overview: Staple cereal grown in flooded or rainfed fields, mainly in the monsoon season.
crops.climate: Warm and humid, roughly 20-35 °C with ample water.
crops.soil: Clay or clay loam that holds water.
crops.irrigation: Needs standing water for much of the season; alternate wetting and drying can save water.
crops.planting: Seedlings raised in a nursery are transplanted after about 3-4 weeks, or seed is direct-sown.
crops.harvest: When most grains in the panicle turn straw-coloured and the lower ones are in the dough stage.
care: Level the field for uniform water depth

pests.name: Blast
pests.symptoms: Diamond-shaped grey-centred lesions on leaves; neck rot.
pests.prevention: Resistant varieties, balanced nitrogen, seed treatment as advised locally.

pests.name: Stem borer
pests.symptoms: Dead hearts in young plants and white ears at heading.
pests.prevention: Remove stubble, use pheromone traps for monitoring, consult an officer for control.

crops.name: Maize
crops.overview: Versatile cereal used for food, feed and industry.
crops.climate: Warm; roughly 21-30 °C. Sensitive to waterlogging and drought at flowering.
crops.irrigation: Critical stages are knee-high, tasseling and silking.
crops.planting: Sown in rows with plant spacing recommended for the variety.
crops.harvest: When husks dry and kernels are hard with a dark layer at the base.

pests.name: Fall armyworm
pests.symptoms: Ragged leaf damage and sawdust-like frass in the whorl.
pests.prevention: Early scouting, timely sowing; seek local guidance on control.

crops.name: Tomato
crops.overview: Popular vegetable crop grown in open fields and protected cultivation.
crops.climate: Warm; fruit set suffers in very hot (above ~35 °C) or cold weather.
crops.soil: Well-drained loam rich in organic matter, pH about 6-7.
crops.irrigation: Regular, even moisture; irregular watering causes fruit cracking.
crops.planting: Seedlings raised in a nursery and transplanted at about 4-5 weeks; staking helps.
crops.harvest: Pick at the stage suited to the market, repeatedly over several weeks.

pests.name: Early blight
pests.symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings on older leaves.
pests.prevention: Crop rotation, remove infected leaves, avoid overhead irrigation.

pests.name: Leaf curl virus (whitefly-borne)
pests.prevention: Control whiteflies, use tolerant varieties, remove infected plants.

crops.name: Potato
crops.overview: Tuber crop grown in cool seasons.
crops.climate: Cool nights favour tuber formation, roughly 15-25 °C.
crops.soil: Loose, well-drained sandy loam, slightly acidic to neutral.
crops.irrigation: Light, frequent irrigation; stop before harvest.
crops.planting: Healthy seed tubers planted in ridges.
crops.harvest: When haulms dry; cure tubers before storage.

pests.name: Late blight
pests.symptoms: Water-soaked dark patches on leaves, white growth underneath in humid weather.
pests.prevention: Healthy seed, resistant varieties, monitor in cool humid weather and ask an officer about protective sprays.

crops.name: Cotton
crops.overview: Fibre crop grown on black and alluvial soils.
crops.climate: Warm, with a long frost-free period.
crops.soil: Deep, well-drained black soil is typical.
crops.irrigation: Needs moisture at flowering and boll development.
crops.planting: Sown at the onset of monsoon with recommended spacing.
crops.harvest: Pick mature, fully opened bolls in several rounds.

pests.name: Pink bollworm
pests.symptoms: Damaged bolls with rosette flowers and stained lint.
pests.prevention: Timely sowing, destroy crop residue, pheromone-trap monitoring, follow local advisories.

crops.name: Sugarcane
crops.overview: Long-duration cash crop for sugar and jaggery.
crops.climate: Warm and humid, with plenty of sunshine.
crops.irrigation: Frequent irrigation, especially in the tillering and grand growth phases.
crops.planting: Setts (stem cuttings) with healthy buds are planted in furrows.
crops.harvest: When cane reaches maturity as advised by the local sugar mill or extension office.

pests.name: Red rot
pests.symptoms: Reddening of internal tissue with whitish patches; sour smell.
pests.prevention: Disease-free setts, resistant varieties, remove and destroy infected clumps.

crops.name: Soybean
crops.overview: Legume oilseed that also fixes nitrogen.
crops.irrigation: Mostly rainfed; critical at flowering and pod filling.
crops.planting: Sown after the monsoon sets in, usually with seed treatment (rhizobium culture).
crops.harvest: When leaves yellow and drop and pods turn brown.
care: Weed control in the first month

pests.name: Yellow mosaic virus
pests.symptoms: Yellow patches on leaves, reduced pod set.
pests.prevention: Tolerant varieties, control whitefly vectors, remove infected plants early.
